subject: Business Models
title: Marketplace Pricing Strategies
description: A 60-second lesson on Marketplace Pricing Strategies.

hook.text: Uber sets the price. Etsy lets sellers set theirs. eBay lets buyers bid. Three pricing models, one goal.

buildup.text: Who controls the price—platform, seller, or buyer—defines the marketplace's power dynamics.

discovery.text: Platform-set pricing creates consistency. Seller-set pricing creates competition. Auctions discover true value.

twist.text: Uber's centralized pricing enraged drivers who couldn't negotiate. But consistent fares built rider trust.

climax.text: Pricing control is the most consequential design decision a marketplace makes. It shapes everything else.

punchline.text: Who sets the price holds the power. That one choice shapes it all.

quiz.question: What's the advantage of platform-controlled pricing?

details.summary: Marketplace pricing strategies include commission on transaction value, subscription fees for sellers, listing fees per item, featured placement fees, and hybrid models..
details.whyItMatters: Pricing strategy determines marketplace economics and sustainability. Charge too much and participants leave the platform. Charge too little and the marketplace cannot fund growth..
takeaways: Commission models take a percentage of each transaction, aligning with participant success
Subscription and listing fees generate predictable revenue independent of transaction volume
Take rates must stay below the cost of participants finding each other independently

faq.question: What is the typical take rate range for marketplaces?
faq.answer: Take rates range from 1 to 3 percent for high-value goods like real estate, 10 to 20 percent for services like ride-sharing and delivery, and 15 to 30 percent for digital goods and app stores. Higher value-add from the marketplace justifies higher take rates.

faq.question: How do marketplaces prevent disintermediation when take rates are high?
faq.answer: They add value through payment processing, dispute resolution, insurance, and escrow. They make the platform essential through reviews and reputation portability. They offer tools that sellers cannot easily replicate. Some use contracts or consequences for off-platform transactions.
